en: Verses in Praise of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Translated by the Śramaṇa Huizhi of the Translation Bureau at Foshouji Temple during the reign of the Empress Dowager of the Tang Dynasty, by Imperial Command.
The Bodhisattva is named Avalokiteśvara; His supernormal powers are unimpeded and immeasurable.
He shakes mountains, dries up oceans, and makes the great earth tremble; Out of compassion for sentient beings, he is of one essence with them.
To remember his name brings fruit that is never in vain; Therefore, one should always invoke and recollect him.
I now sincerely contemplate those virtues and praise the Bodhisattva with a heart of reverence;
his wisdom is as deep as the ocean, and his skillful means are unfathomable.
Among all the devas, asuras, mahoragas, and the multitudes of humans, none can measure them.
All have praised [the Buddha] with subtle, wondrous, and pure verses, never wearying throughout kalpas;
now I shall proclaim these "Verses of Spring," describing but a small portion of his merits.
Among those of worldly form who are dignified and majestic, none among the devas surpasses Brahmā.
How much less can the natural form-body of the Sage’s sovereign power compare—hundreds of thousands of millions of parts do not equal one!
The Venerable One’s head-ornaments are most magnificent and beautiful;
crowned with *māndārava* flowers and golden blossoms, adorned with the lovely splendor of rainbows, they further resemble the crescent moon reflected upon the king of mountains.
Furthermore, he resembles Mount Sumeru formed of a hundred jewels; the Venerable One’s physical form is most subtle and wondrous.
Like a light rain enshrouding a jeweled peak, his shoulders are draped with the colors of the *aineya* deer;
his radiance is brilliant and all-pervading, towering and preeminent like a mountain of gold.
Like the full moon dwelling in the void, And resembling the color of the campaka flower,
surpassing the body of Maheśvara; Adorned merely with white nāgas as a necklace,
holding a golden lotus in his right hand, With a stem made of vaiḍūrya gemstone.
With compassion, he causes to bloom flowers of supreme fragrance and purity, which inspire love and joy in all the wise.

These most excellent and pure flowers held in the hands of the Honored One are adorned with exquisite beauty and profound radiance, like the moonlight shining upon the summit of Mount Sumeru; they serve as the lotus pedestals upon which his holy body abides.
Moved by the merit of the Venerable One, I, with a heart of utmost sincerity and devotion,
take refuge and pay homage to the one who grants boons; to him praised by the offerings of the devas,
I now pay homage with a pure mind— to the Venerable Śrīgupta, whose hair is like a black bee.
The Sage’s wondrous image dwells within it; its radiance shines forth, adorning his venerable head like scorched coral or the color of flashing lightning.
Furthermore, it is like orpiment illuminating the Black Mountains, adorning the Great Sage’s body from top to bottom. I venture to compose these words to praise him.
When fierce elephants with sharp tusks surround one from all four sides, and a person therein is about to be harmed—
if that person focuses their mind on the Bodhisattva— they will abandon suffering and distress and remain fearless.
Even when a violent dragon roars and emits poisonous smoke, snarling in rage with a fierce and evil countenance, [the devotee remains unafraid].
When about to be devoured by such a person, it is truly terrifying; yet by recollecting Avalokiteśvara, one is immediately liberated.

When the ocean tides and wind-waves roar with sound, and the great makara fish all tremble and surge, if a person’s boat is wrecked and they fall into its midst, by recollecting that Avalokiteśvara, they obtain peace and security.
In high mountains, perilous valleys, and amidst hanging cliffs, where rushing streams splash against rocks in places of many hardships—
if a person falls therein with no one to offer rescue, they shall call upon Avalokiteśvara in their heart and reach the other shore.
When fierce flames of a raging fire and violent winds arise, spreading their conflagration through houses and burning people, [they shall likewise reach safety].
If one mindfully recollects that treasury of merit with a sincere heart, the calamitous fires of the moment shall not cause harm.
Even if a person is bound in prison, their body encumbered by shackles, manacles, and fetters,
because they sincerely invoke the name of Avalokiteśvara, that person shall be liberated in an instant.
If a person falls into a great pit of fire, And single-mindedly invokes the name of Avalokiteśvara,
That person will be freed from heat and attain purity, Just like a lotus flower blooming in a pond.
If a person passes through a vast forest And suddenly encounters thunder, lightning, and torrential rain,
When thunderbolts are about to strike and one is in extreme peril, by invoking the name of Avalokiteśvara, one escapes disaster.
If a person encounters a fierce lion with fangs and claws as sharp as swords,
glaring with rage and roaring to devour them, by invoking the name of Avalokiteśvara, they shall be spared harm.
The evil bandits, the Mlecchas of the Turks, are fierce and treacherous, devoid of compassion like rākṣasas;
they bind people with iron chains. Yet by invoking the name and directing one's thoughts [to the Buddha], all are liberated.
In deep mountains, vast marshes, and perilous places, where robbers lie in wait to plunder and seize, [the Buddha’s power provides protection].
If one recites the name and maintains the power of mindfulness, praying for protection, that person will be set free from affliction and suffering.
Even if others cast spells, engage in slander, or plot injury, constantly seeking means through an evil mind,
because that person constantly remembers and contemplates Avalokiteśvara, they shall ultimately be unable to cause harm.
In the midst of battle, where banners and drums face one another and the clash of blades and arrows leaves a trail of severed limbs,
if at that moment one brings the name to mind, the Bodhisattva bestows fearlessness therein. Even when powerful,
malevolent spirits or *kumbhāṇḍas* seize a person to drink their marrow, [the Bodhisattva provides protection].
If one can fix the mind on Avalokiteśvara, that person will be protected against pestilence,
demonic diseases, fevers, abdominal distension, consumption, jaundice, heart disease,
leprosy, epilepsy, cholera, and various ailments such as blood disorders and emaciation.
When various evil and dark karmas entangle their bodies, by invoking the name and maintaining mindfulness, all are healed and cured.
There are hungry ghosts whose bellies are like mountains, their lips and mouths parched and withered, tormented by hunger and thirst;
when the Bodhisattva sees them, he gives rise to compassion and causes them to attain full satisfaction in succession.
When hungry ghosts are oppressed by cold and frost, their bodies and skin are utterly destroyed;
as they raise both hands in extreme agony, through supernatural power and skillful means, they are made comfortable and warm.
Just as the Golden-Winged Bird (Garuda) uses its beak and talons to seize dragons from the water and land, so too does he deliver them.
If that dragon concentrates its mind on the Bodhisattva, it shall immediately be freed from suffering and obtain peace and happiness.
If there are those who desire to seek superior rewards— such as elephants, horses, chariots,
servants, clothing, food and drink, and various precious jewels— it is because they constantly keep Avalokiteśvara in mind.
Their prayers and aspirations shall be spontaneously fulfilled;
if there are those who wish to attain the art of longevity, they may sit or lie amidst the clouds, traveling at will through the void.
Because they constantly recollect and contemplate Avalokiteśvara, they shall obtain divine mantras and elixirs of immortality. Thus have I beheld the image of Avalokiteśvara depicted upon the wall.
Beholding all the marks and signs of physical form and their various virtues, and seeing his great mastery of supernatural powers, I have given rise to sincere praise.
All the various virtues that exist are foremost among those of the Bodhisattvas; they possess boundless skillful means and great expedients.
Manifesting a pure and wondrous form-body, Far removed from all conceptualizations of existence and non-existence,
Benefiting immeasurable beings like space— By this praise of the treasury of merit,
I pray that you may realize the omniscience of a Tathāgata. Through this praise of the supreme merits of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, may it serve as a sublime support.
May Your Majesty, the Sage and Divine Emperor, the Sovereign of the Nation, skillfully turn the Golden Wheel.
May your physical vigor and lifespan be forever inexhaustible,
and may your wisdom and its karmic fruition be inconceivable.
May you eternally govern Jambudvīpa and dwell long in China,
protecting the Triple Gem and benefiting all sentient beings,
so that every living creature may receive your holy blessings.
